title: MEPS denial and prior-authorization friction persists across observed care channels
source_unit: MEPS 2024 people with a first dated office, emergency-room, or inpatient event joined to annual institutional-friction and household-context fields

observations.period: 2024; first office event × insurance denial or prior-authorization delay

denominator.unit: valid friction-group people among first dated office-event people; outcome-specific valid rows vary

observations.method: Select first valid dated office event per person, exact-join to HC-256 by DUPERSID+PANEL, and compare EQDENY53 groups using positive PERWT24F.
observations.uncertainty: EQDENY53 is annual and has no claim identifier, decision date, appeal, or resolution; denial timing relative to the office event is unknown. Same-round outcomes are context, not effects.
observations.subgroup: First dated office-event people with valid denial/delay status.
observations.counterinterpretation: Complex care, health severity, coverage, prior debt, and service selection may generate both friction and the observed context.

related_sources.claim: The method note defines the event-family join and the claim-level timing/remedy boundary.
The machine output preserves input hashes, event-family denominators, and weighted group outcomes.

boundary: This is a same-round event-family stratification of institutional-friction associations. It does not show that denial preceded the event, caused care delay or debt, or produced a remedy, trust change, political action, or exit.
